terms.gloss: court, pay attention to, cultivate (a person)
evidence: Cic. Att. 2.19.5: colere aliquem, beside observāre (Lewis & Short s.v. observō)
Traupman p. 105: play up to s.o., aliquem colō
terms.comment: To “cultivate” a person: attend on him, show him respect, often with an eye to his favour. It is not necessarily insincere; for open flattery, assentārī and blandīrī are the words.

sources: Lewis & Short: colo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 105, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
